title: Stand straight as you were commanded.
subtitle: Steadiness without going beyond the limits

row.title: the Prophet ﷺ
sub: and those who turned with him

then: After all the stories, Allah commands the Prophet ﷺ and the believers with him to {idea}stand firm and upright, as commanded{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says this is a great help against opposition. He also forbids transgression, which {trap}destroys the one who does it, even against a polytheist{/trap}. Allah sees all they do.
now: You start strong in Ramadan, then crash. Or you get angry online and go further than truth allows. {idea}Straight is steady, not extreme.{/idea} Keep the line, every day, and do not cross it even when provoked.
old: Being religious means going as hard as I can.
new: Allah asks me to stay straight and steady, and never cross limits, even with those I oppose.
try: Choose one small act of worship you can keep daily, and keep it the same size all week.

title: Do not lean toward those who do wrong.
subtitle: Small compromises with wrong add up
then: Ibn Abbas explained the verse: {trap}do not compromise with them, do not side with those who do wrong{/trap}. Ibn Kathir adds: do not seek their help, as if approving their evil. Otherwise {idea}you will have no protector besides Allah{/idea} and no one to help you.
now: Your friend is running a dodgy scheme and asks you to just "vouch for him." Your boss wants your quiet support for something unfair. {trap}Leaning starts small.{/trap} You can be kind to people and still refuse to prop up what they are doing wrong.
old: As long as I am not the one doing wrong, supporting it a little is fine.
new: Leaning on wrongdoing, even quietly, pulls me toward it; Allah is my only real protector.
try: Decline one request today that would mean quietly backing something you know is wrong.

title: Good deeds wash away bad ones.
subtitle: Prayer through the day as a cleansing river
then: Ibn Mas'ud reported that a man who had kissed a woman not lawful to him came to the Prophet ﷺ, ashamed. This verse came: {idea}establish prayer at both ends of the day and in the night{/idea}, for {reward}good deeds remove misdeeds{/reward}. He asked if it was only for him. The Prophet ﷺ said it was for all his community.
now: You said something cruel this afternoon, or looked at something you should not have. Now you feel too dirty to pray. {reward}That is exactly when to pray.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ compared the five prayers to a river at your door you bathe in five times a day.
old: After I sin, I should stay away from prayer until I feel worthy.
new: Prayer and good deeds are how Allah washes my sins away, so I go to them right after a slip.
try: The next time you slip today, make wudu and pray two rakat right away.

title: Be patient; no good effort is ever lost.
subtitle: Patience alongside prayer
then: Right after the command to pray, Allah says {idea}be patient{/idea}. The believers in Makkah faced rejection and pressure every day. {reward}Allah does not let the reward of those who do good be lost.{/reward}
now: You keep showing up: caring for an ill parent, raising a child alone, working an honest job that pays less. Months pass with no thanks. {reward}Not one hour is wasted.{/reward} Patience is trusting that it is all being kept.
old: If my efforts go unnoticed, they were pointless.
new: Allah keeps every good effort I make, so my patience is never wasted.
try: Write down one hard thing you keep doing for Allah's sake, and remind yourself: none of it is lost.

title: If only a few had spoken up against corruption.
subtitle: The missing voices in the past nations
then: Allah asks why there were not, among earlier generations, {idea}people of wisdom who forbade corruption on earth{/idea}, except a few whom He saved. The wrongdoers {trap}chased the luxuries they were given{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says this is why this community is told to always have people who call to good and forbid evil.
now: Someone in the office shares a cruel joke about a colleague. Your cousin is cheating his business partner and everyone knows. {idea}One calm voice matters.{/idea} Silence feels safe, but the few who spoke were the ones saved.
old: It is not my place to say anything when others do wrong.
new: A few people willing to speak gently against wrong can protect a whole community.
try: When you see something wrong today, say one kind, clear sentence about it instead of staying silent.

title: He would never destroy a town of reformers.
subtitle: Reformers protect the places they live in
then: Allah says He {idea}would not destroy towns unjustly while their people were reformers{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains that no punishment comes to a town unless its people wronged themselves, and {reward}your Lord is not unjust to His servants{/reward}.
now: Your street, your workplace, your family group. Someone has to be the one who fixes, forgives, picks up litter, settles the quarrel. {reward}Reformers protect the places they live in.{/reward} You can be one of them.
old: What happens to my community has nothing to do with me.
new: When people work to set things right, they become a protection for the place they live.
try: Do one small repair in your community today: settle a dispute, clean a space, help a neighbor.

title: He could have made everyone one community.
subtitle: Why people keep differing
then: Allah says that {idea}had He willed, He could have made mankind one community{/idea}, all upon belief. Ibn Kathir says instead {trap}people will always differ in religions, creeds and opinions{/trap}. This comes after a whole surah of nations that chose differently from their prophets.
now: You look at your family and see every view under one roof: devout, doubting, indifferent. It frustrates you. {idea}Difference was allowed for a reason.{/idea} Choice is real, which means your own choice to follow guidance really counts.
old: If Allah wanted everyone guided, nobody would disagree.
new: Allah allowed people to differ so that choosing guidance is a real choice, including mine.
try: In your next disagreement about faith, focus on your own choice to follow guidance rather than on winning.

title: Except those your Lord has shown mercy.
subtitle: The way out of endless division

row.title: following the Prophet ﷺ
sub: what he and his Companions were upon

then: People will keep differing {reward}except those your Lord has shown mercy{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says these are the ones who follow the messengers and what they commanded. Asked who the saved group are, the Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}those upon what I and my Companions are upon{/idea}. And {trap}Allah's word that He will fill Hell{/trap} will be fulfilled.
now: Online, everyone is in a camp, fighting over labels and personalities. You feel the pull to pick a side and defend it. {idea}Mercy is in following the Prophet ﷺ{/idea}, not in winning the group argument.
old: The right group is the one I already belong to.
new: Mercy comes from following what the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were upon, not from loyalty to a camp.
try: Before sharing a religious opinion online, check what the Prophet ﷺ actually said on it.

title: These stories were told to steady your heart.
subtitle: Why the surah gathered all these prophets
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that He related all these stories of the messengers {idea}to make his heart firm{/idea}. They show how the prophets were rejected and harmed, and how Allah helped the believers. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said "in this" means this surah: it brings {reward}the truth, an admonition, and a reminder for the believers{/reward}.
now: You feel alone in trying to live your faith: the only one praying at the office, the only one in the family who fasts. {idea}Read the stories again.{/idea} Nuh, Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, Musa all stood where you stand, and they were helped.
old: No one has ever faced what I am facing.
new: The prophets faced it before me, and their stories are there to steady my heart.
try: Reread one prophet's story from this surah tonight and note one thing that steadies you.

title: Keep to your way. We are working on ours.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ echoes the prophets before him
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to say to the deniers what Shu'ayb said earlier: {trap}act according to your way{/trap}, {idea}we are acting on ours{/idea}. Ibn Kathir calls it a warning, and notes that Allah fulfilled His promise and helped His Messenger ﷺ.
now: Your relatives tease you every Eid about how "strict" you have become. You have explained, more than once. {idea}Now you just keep going.{/idea} Your consistency is your answer.
old: I have to convince everyone before I can be at peace with my choices.
new: Once I have spoken clearly, I can simply keep working on my path and let time show.
try: Skip one argument today and instead do one good deed you were going to do anyway.

title: Wait, and we are waiting too.
subtitle: Calm waiting for how things end
then: The command continues: {idea}wait, we too are waiting{/idea}. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse that the wrongdoers will not succeed. He says {reward}Allah fulfilled His promise to His Messenger ﷺ{/reward}, helped him, and made His word uppermost.
now: You are waiting for the job offer, the test result, the reconciliation with a sibling. Waiting can eat you up. {reward}A believer's waiting is calm{/reward}, because it is waiting on a promise from One who keeps His word.
old: Waiting means sitting in anxiety until things work out.
new: I can wait calmly, because I am waiting on Allah, who keeps His promises.
try: While you wait on something today, replace one anxious thought with: Allah keeps His promise.

title: Every matter returns to Him; worship and trust Him.
subtitle: The last words of Surah Hud
then: Surah Hud ends here. {idea}To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth{/idea}, and every matter returns to Him. So worship Him and rely on Him. Ibn Kathir says {reward}He is sufficient for whoever trusts and turns to Him{/reward}, and nothing anyone does is hidden from Him.
now: You close the app after a heavy surah full of floods, cries and ruins. Your own worries are still there: rent, kids, health. {reward}Hand them over.{/reward} Worship Him, trust Him, and know He sees every effort you make.
old: I have to carry all of my worries and hold everything together myself.
new: Everything returns to Allah, so I worship Him, rely on Him, and trust He sees what I do.
try: Tonight, name your three biggest worries to Allah in dua and say: I rely on You.
